full local pytest regression, 3 reports/tests suites

requirement_results.command: two DISTINCT commands racing the same aggregate/expected_revision on real PostgreSQL connections: exactly one succeeds, the other raises a real revision-conflict error; an independent connection directly observes the real advisory lock held by the other session during the race (not merely inferred from the outcome)

a concurrent reader on an independent connection, sampling continuously throughout a live distinct-writer race, never observes a revision value outside the valid boundary set -- no dirty read of an uncommitted or torn write is ever leaked under READ COMMITTED

a real process crash (subprocess, os._exit after inserting but before commit) is deterministically synchronized -- via an independent probe polling the real advisory lock -- to be genuinely in flight when a second, live writer concurrently attempts the same aggregate/expected_revision; the survivor commits successfully once the crashed transaction's lock is released, and the reconciled ledger accepts further correct progress afterward

assert_atomic_visibility() (the sealed reconciliation oracle from OCOR-DEV-0015) reports zero anomalies after every real-concurrency scenario above, and a synthetic phantom_receipt anomaly (an idempotency row whose receipt references a non-existent commit) falsifies it, proving negative_acceptance_criteria: a phantom receipt or unreconciled commit is detected, never silently accepted
full local pytest regression, no new failures versus the pre-existing sandbox baseline (the two known interpreter-pin failures are unrelated and pre-existing)

residual_risks: This spike's oracles all target the SAME PostgreSQL backend already implemented and sealed by OCOR-DEV-0015; it does not evaluate an alternative backend, consistent with the task's 'selected backend' framing and its migration_and_compatibility_procedure (no architecture substitution).

The failure-under-concurrency scenario relies on a real advisory-lock contention probe to synchronize the crash with a live concurrent writer deterministically; if that synchronization primitive itself were ever unsound, the test asserts loudly on the contention-observed precondition rather than silently passing on a lucky race, so it cannot regress into a false-positive concurrency proof.

The isolation oracle empirically samples revision values during a live race under this database's default READ COMMITTED isolation level; it does not attempt to characterize behavior under a different isolation level, since the C3 store does not request one.

The same pre-existing local-venv gap noted in prior evidence (uv cannot resolve the exact 3.12.11 interpreter in this sandbox) is unchanged and out of this task's scope; it no longer affects PostgreSQL-backed tests now that OCOR_LIVE_POSTGRES_DSN can be set locally against the ocor-bootstrap stack.
rollback_procedure_verified: Every scenario begins from oracle.reset() (a real TRUNCATE against the live schema) and ends with assert_atomic_visibility() reporting a fully consistent state; the failure-under-concurrency scenario is itself a real rollback drill -- a genuine process crash mid-transaction, followed by a live proof that zero partial state survived and that the ledger continues correctly afterward.
